report:
No plan has been adopted; nothing is settled. I made no legal decisions and moved no money.

All concerns from the initial needs round have confirmed NCEs:
- A: a dependable sense of when the trailer will be available for making plans; stating needs plainly despite neighbor/coworker awkwardness; the storage NCE (not having to guess where the trailer will be, and any storage change is something A can say no to before counting on it).
- C: the home project keeping moving with dependable hauling soon; C's need being considered in its own right rather than ranked below A's by default; stating needs plainly despite awkward relationships; the same storage NCE.
- B: her place staying usable and the trailer not being in her way; landlord approval before any pad change is relied on; no one counting on a pad change before B has asked her landlord and said yes or no herself; being able to name what isn't working, including felt responsibility, without being put in the middle; being able to raise an awkward need without managing everyone else's reactions.
- Mine, confirmed by A, B and C: each person can have concerns understood, speak up, and say no—even a small no—before anything is settled; and my help stays to listening, reflecting needs, and drafting options for validation, not deciding rights or money.

I drafted options and brought them back for validation, with guardrails: no storage change assumed, B not messenger/middle/tie-breaker, no one asked to back down, neither A's nor C's needs ranked by default. As a participant, I stated disagreement with any option that violates those needs. Silence has not been treated as agreement.

Validation is incomplete. C said no to Option 2 as written: C needs actual dates and a dependable hauling turn in the next few weeks, not merely after A's; Option 1 is only a step; C would not accept a tie-break that leaves the project waiting. B said Option 1 is okay only as a step and only if sharing B's concerns stays optional; Option 4 is okay but not as a final answer; B cannot yet say yes to Options 2 or 3, and her landlord has not been asked, so no one may count on the trailer moving from her pad. A has not replied to the validation draft. No option has three yeses.

I record these as unresolved, not agreed: C's new no about dated, dependable hauling; B's condition that sharing concerns stay optional; A's validation; B's and C's fuller validation of the revised options. Those new concerns still need the same what-matters/why, tentative NCE, and wording check before being recorded as settled. The landlord/storage question also remains unresolved.
